payload.text:
Don't merge this yet. The main feature doesn't work: overlapping imports still come out with duplicate contacts.

**Blocker: `dedupe` checks whether two entries are the same object, not whether they have the same id** (`src/dedupe.js`)
```js
return [...new Set(contacts)];
```
A `Set` only treats two entries as duplicates if they are literally the same object in memory. The README says identity is the id, "never object identity." Two overlapping imports produce separate objects with the same id, so nothing gets removed. I checked it:
```
mergeImports([{id:1,name:'A'}], [{id:1,name:'A'}])
→ [ { id: 1, name: 'A' }, { id: 1, name: 'A' } ]
```
A fix that keeps the first contact seen for each id, as the README says:
```js
function dedupe(contacts) {
  const seen = new Set();
  return contacts.filter((c) => !seen.has(c.id) && seen.add(c.id));
}
```

**The tests don't catch this** (`test/dedupe.test.js`)
- The first test reuses one object (`[a, a]`), which is the only case a `Set` handles. Add a test with two separate objects that share an id, and check that the first one is kept, e.g. `[{id:1,name:'Ada'}, {id:1,name:'Ada L.'}]` should become just `[{id:1,name:'Ada'}]`.
- `mergeImports` has no tests. Add one with two lists that overlap.

**Minor**
- `byName` (`src/order.js`) looks good: it copies the list before sorting, so the input is left alone, and contacts with no name sort first. Its test covers this.
- Contacts with no `id` would all be treated as one contact by the fix above. If that can happen in real imports, decide how to handle it.
- The CHANGELOG entry, version bump to 2.2.0 and README sections are fine. They'll be accurate once dedupe is fixed.

Once the dedupe fix and the duplicate-id test are in, it's good to merge. I didn't change anything on the branch.
